plain: The wall asks for a clock with a rate and a unit, but the unit is already a registered primitive and an overall rate is a relabelling that no record statistic can see. The two 2026-08-11 witnesses (formation probability 1/3 vs 2/3, parallel vs sequential completion) are one phenomenon, namely whether neighbouring sites may form at the same instant; once that is excluded, the only physical content is a probability measure on formation orders plus rate ratios between regions. That hands the residue to the formation-order wall T01 and the lapse question (T64/L14) and derives no clock.
best_route: R1: treat formation events as a trace over the adjacency dependence graph (concurrency theory), so laws depend only on the acyclic orientation and Foata depth is a unit-free clock; it ends at an orientation measure, blocked-equivalent to T01.
test: test_T11.py (exact/float, 6 graphs to the 8-site cube, plus a 12-ring hop chain): permutation classes = acyclic orientations (4,8,14,8,64,1862) with equal laws inside classes; parallel-kernel witness sits at L1 distance (3/5)q/(2-q) from the hull of ordered laws on two sites (0.225 at q=2/3 on the 7-site star) and tends to random-sequential as q->0; rate ratios change the final law, a common scale does not; once-only formation depth is 13.8 / 2 / 28 for i.i.d. / checkerboard / sweep orders at L=10; hops keep the Gibbs law on commuting layers (TV 1e-14) and lose it on simultaneous layers (TV 0.090).
cheaper_question: Which probability measure on acyclic orientations of the forming set (with which rate-ratio field between regions) does the formation law induce, and is co-formation of adjacent sites excluded (H1)? Units are already registered; the absolute rate is gauge.
